conventions.convention: Natural units c = ℏ = 1, mostly-plus Minkowski metric, global gauge group SU(2), connection-normalized adjoint scalar, and no microscopic matter hypermultiplets. Eight-supercharge invariance is adopted, not proved.

Classical vacuum moduli retain all simultaneous F/D-zero compact-group orbits with quotient topology. Quantum vacuum rays require an already constructed Hilbert-space theory and normalized translation-invariant vectors annihilated by every supercharge and adjoint.
The formal label lattice is Z² with ordered labels (n_e,n_m) and pairing Z_SW = n_e a + n_m a_D. Labels do not imply particle existence, stability, or an allowed line operator.
The period column is (a_D,a); magnetic and electric cycles have intersection +1. The scalar algebraic central charge is z = √2 Z_SW. Periods and prepotentials are local and may be multivalued.

The local charged scalars have dual charges +1 and −1; their kinetic terms are canonical, while the neutral and Maxwell coefficients use g_D⁻². Freezing the metric and replacing u by its linear Taylor polynomial are separate approximations.

Winding n is nonzero. The coefficient of dθ in the pulled-back A − d arg M tends uniformly to zero. Original electric flux means dual magnetic flux in the selected model dictionary. An admitted profile need not solve field equations.

The nonlinear variational class confines the neutral scalar to a closed valid disk with u′ nonzero, supplies a smooth uniformly positive bounded metric, assumes uniform vacuum approach, and uses static A_0 = 0 with constant or absent theta. Cylinder end traces are canonical exterior representatives; normal A_3 is unrestricted.

Generic nonlinear confinement concerns positive planar infima and I_n(L)/L → τ_n; attainment and an O(1) remainder are not claimed. Exact critical tension and O(1) cylinder bounds require the linear-superpotential, constant-metric branch.

load_bearing.statement: On the specified local monopole patch, with canonical charged fields and frozen metric b = g_D⁻², W_mu = √2 A_D M Mtilde + μu(A_D), and V_mu = g_D²|∂_A_D W_mu|² + |∂_M W_mu|² + |∂_Mtilde W_mu|² + D²/2, where D = g_D(|M|² − |Mtilde|²). The linear-u truncation is an additional approximation.

Assume full Axiom of Choice and the defined nonlinear local magnetostatic data, bounded positive metric, compact neutral disk, uniform vacuum approach and constant or absent theta. Then V_b ≥ c_V(s − ξ)², E_b ≥ γ2πξ|n|, every nonzero-winding class is nonempty, and 0 < τ_n < ∞. Canonical profiles admit finite-energy fixed-width collars, giving τ_n L ≤ I_n(L) ≤ (τ_n + ε)(L − 2ℓ) + C_ε and consequently I_n(L)/L → τ_n > 0.

Assume full Axiom of Choice and the constant-metric linear truncation u(A_D) = u_m + cA_D, with cμ nonzero. Every specified finite-energy winding-n profile obeys E ≥ 2πξ|n|. For every nonzero winding and effective divisor of degree |n|, the mathematical vortex supplier gives an embedded stationary absolute full-model transverse minimum with tension T_n = 2πξ|n|. Fixed canonical end traces admit actual collars and I_L = T_n L + O(1). Generic nonlinear u instead has the stated neutral-field stationarity obstruction.

Adopt the source-proposed pure SU(2) N=2 two-derivative solution: the specified genus-one family and differential, local periods and monodromies, central-charge normalization z = √2(n_e a + n_m a_D), and one monopole patch with A_D = a_D, a_D(u_m) = 0 and a_D′(u_m) nonzero. This is adopted low-energy model data, not a continuum construction.

For the specified finite-dimensional canonical rigid gauge-model data with no FI term, classical supersymmetric vacuum configurations are simultaneous zeros of every F_i and D_a, and the classical vacuum-moduli set is their compact-group orbit quotient. Quantum vacuum-moduli data are defined separately and conditionally on a constructed theory.

If a finite-energy dual vortex profile of winding n ∈ Z\{0} exists under the specified smoothness and boundary conditions, then Φ_D = 2πn and 0 < σ < ∞. No existence, stability, or minimizing confining potential follows.

concerns.concern: Proof 3.1 defines G(R) as the circle integral of |Dq|² + |Dp|² and immediately infers integrability of G over radii from finite planar energy. This needs the polar-coordinate decomposition, including ds = R dθ. The declared Fubini supplier alone supplies no Cartesian-to-polar change of measure. The published polar-coordinate theorem and its surface-measure convention were opened and provide an available justification; this is a small missing proof-support step.

Proof 2.1 says '[F9] and finite energy give' integrability over R of the circle-gradient integral G(R). F9 is Fubini, whose statement does not establish polar-coordinate decomposition or the circle arc-length factor. Supply that elementary derivation or identify the exact polar-coordinate supplier. The outside critical-minimum proof explicitly supplies this conversion, whereas this proof does not.
